verdict.rationale: Dynadot's security page documents two-factor authentication, account lock, and optional Registry Lock, so the 2FA part of account defensibility is covered by a single first-party mention. Nothing in the evidence shows scoped or least-privilege API credentials or IP allowlisting on API access, which is most of the story. Missing for 10: scoped/permissioned API keys, IP allowlisting for API access, detail on 2FA methods (TOTP or hardware keys), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the registrar account itself is defensible — real 2FA, scoped API credentials, and IP allowlisting on API access

citations.quote: Dynadot offers free domain privacy, account lock, two-factor authentication, and optional Registry Lock to keep your online assets safe.
